turns.assessment: The simultaneous outage of many unrelated services and protection switching localizes the fault to their sole common working-path element, E1 (roadm.S01). Concurrent AMP_INPUT_LOS on two different lines leaving S01 and widespread OCH_LOS indicate loss within the optical layer at S01, not an individual client, transponder, span, or OTN switch fault. A failed WSS input port can block the common arriving channels before they are routed onto multiple outgoing degrees, matching the pattern.

proposals.rationale: roadm.S01 is the only element shared by every affected working path. A WSS input-port failure there explains simultaneous channel loss across multiple outgoing degrees, including AMP_INPUT_LOS on S01->S04 and S01->S15, while unchanged amplifier pump currents argue against amplifier failures.
A switch-fabric failure at the common site could interrupt many ODUs, but it should produce ODU_AIS rather than widespread optical OCH_LOS and amplifier input loss, so it is strongly disfavored.
proposals.note: site named; its node equipment does not document the mode

clarify.assessment: The evidence localizes the fault to a WSS input port at roadm.S01, but does not identify which incoming degree. The AMP_INPUT_LOS alarms on multiple outgoing degrees are compatible with blockage of channels from any one of these input ports, and unchanged upstream optical monitoring does not distinguish a port-local failure among them.
